subject: Constrain only one element of a vector

messages.author: fde4048c840328bf
messages.subject: Constrain only one element of a vector
parts:
Hi,

Suppose that under Parameters, I want to define a vector of parameters (for example, the betas in a linear regression). If I know that one (and only one) of the elements of the vector is going to have for sure a support [0,1] (for example), is it possible to constrain only that element of the vector?

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Constrain only one element of a vector
parts:
On 1/29/13 1:53 PM, cmg82 wrote:
> Suppose that under Parameters, I want to define a vector of parameters (for example, the betas in a linear regression).
> If I know that one (and only one) of the elements of the vector is going to have for sure a support [0,1] (for example),
> is it possible to constrain only that element of the vector?

Not directly, but you can do it indirectly. Suppose
you want a total of N and the first is constrained.

parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> x1;
real x2_N[N-1];
}
transformed parameters {
real x[N];
x[1] <- x1;
for (n in 1:(N-1))
x[n+1] <- x2_N[n];
}
... now use x ...

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Constrain only one element of a vector
parts:
This has come up a few times, but I'm afraid we
don't have a good way to do that. All of the
variables in an array or vector or matrix get the
same constraint.

You could define the transforms yourself if you add
the log Jacobian determinant. See the chapter of the manual
on how we do it internally.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Constrain only one element of a vector
parts:
On Saturday, March 23, 2013 12:19:27 PM UTC-4, rubi wrote:
The constraints are a vector of constants read in the data part:
vector[G] C;

And what I want is that:
parameters {
  vector[G] sigma: //where sigma[g] is constrained between lower=0 and upper=C[g], for every g in G
}

It is not currently possible to use a vector of upper bounds. What you can do is

data {
  vector[G] C;
}
parameters {
  vector<lower=0, upper = 1>[G] sigma_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[G] sigma;
  sigma <- sigma_raw * C;
}

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Constrain only one element of a vector
parts: This is almost certainly a bad idea.

> On Oct 17, 2016, at 7:32 PM, Stefano <mangiol...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> I have a question related to this:
>
> What about if C is a parameter. Would a parameter depending on another create problems of high correlation?
>
>
> parameters {
> vector[G] C;
> vector<lower=0, upper = 1>[G] sigma_raw;
> }
> transformed parameters {
> vector[G] sigma;
> sigma <- sigma_raw * C;
> }

This isn't going to work because sigma_raw and C aren't
independently identified, only their product is. If you
try to put a prior on C, if it shrinks toward 0, sigma_raw
will be driven to 1 and you'll get all kinds of sampling
problems due to the boundaries and non-identifiability.

I would very strongly recommend just using:

vector<lower=0>[G] sigma;

and imposing a prior directly on sigma.

- Bob
